title: Elephant Poaching Fell 61%, But Herds Remain 77% Smaller
hook: Elephant poaching plunged, but the population collapse remains.
closing: Lower poaching helps, but rebuilding elephant herds requires protection that lasts for generations.
question: Should ivory sales stay banned?

segments.say: African elephant numbers fell 77%. More than three quarters disappeared despite their iconic status.
African elephants fell from 1.3 million to 0.415 million. The surviving population remains a fraction of its former size.
Elephant poaching fell from 10.1% to 3.9% yearly. Stronger ivory controls sharply reduced the killing rate.
